title: Psalm 58: There Is Surely a God Who Judges
summary: David confronts corrupt rulers who pervert justice, describes the wicked as liars from birth and deaf as a cobra, and asks God to break their teeth and make them vanish. The psalm ends with the righteous rejoicing at God's vengeance and all people confessing that there is a God who judges the earth.

from.where: The Study Bible's notes on Psalm 58
from.text: It belongs to a group of psalms often called imprecatory

line: David confronts rulers who pervert justice and asks God to break the power of the wicked, ending with the confession that there is a God who judges the earth.
guide: It is a cry from people crushed by those meant to protect them, not a pattern for how to feel about people you dislike. If you have been wronged like that, bring your anger to God in words as strong as you need, and leave the judging to him. If you hold any power over others, its first question is for you.

care.text: The book page's part on the cursing psalms sets out four ways Christians read lines like these: as honest prayer that hands vengeance to God instead of taking it; as the voice of people crushed by injustice; as prayers changed by the cross, where Jesus prayed for those who killed him; and as words Scripture records honestly but that are not for Christian lips. Thoughtful believers hold each view, and these notes do not choose between them. One thing is not open: no reading of this psalm has ever made it right to harm anyone.

stanzas.title: Liars from birth, deaf as a cobra
A prayer that God would break their power
The righteous rejoice: there is a God who judges

verses.t: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “Do Not Destroy.” A Miktam of David. Do you indeed speak justly, O rulers? Do you judge uprightly, O sons of men?
No, in your hearts you devise injustice; with your hands you mete out violence on the earth.
The wicked are estranged from the womb; the liars go astray from birth.
Their venom is like the venom of a snake, like a cobra that shuts its ears,
refusing to hear the tune of the charmer who skillfully weaves his spell.
O God, shatter their teeth in their mouths; O LORD, tear out the fangs of the lions.
May they vanish like water that runs off; when they draw the bow, may their arrows be blunted.
Like a slug that dissolves in its slime, like a woman’s stillborn child, may they never see the sun.
Before your pots can feel the burning thorns— whether green or dry— He will sweep them away.
The righteous will rejoice when they see they are avenged; they will wash their feet in the blood of the wicked.
Then men will say, “There is surely a reward for the righteous! There is surely a God who judges the earth!”
